papers.title: HIT-MAP: A scalable approach to multimodal mapping of subcellular organization.
papers.abstract: Multimodal mapping of subcellular protein organization through imaging and interaction proteomics has been mostly confined to large consortia, owing to high per-target costs, reliance on target-specific antibodies or libraries of epitope-tagged cDNAs, and the lack of unified pipelines for coordinated data acquisition. Here, we present HIT-MAP (high-throughput integrated tagging for cell mapping), an end-to-end framework that couples endogenous epitope tagging with optimized wide-field immunofluorescence imaging and affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS). Applied to a pilot set of 16 r
papers.summary: HIT-MAP is an end-to-end framework that combines endogenous epitope tagging, optimized wide-field immunofluorescence imaging, and affinity purification-mass spectrometry to map subcellular protein organization in a coordinated, scalable way. By avoiding target-specific antibodies and cDNA libraries, it lowers the cost and complexity that previously restricted multimodal subcellular mapping to large consortia. The authors demonstrate the approach on a pilot set of 16 targets.

papers.title: Defining the Genetic and Phenotypic Landscape of Primary Immune Regulatory Disorders Using the ClinGen Validation Framework.
papers.abstract: Primary immune regulatory disorders (PIRDs) represent a rapidly growing group of inborn errors of immunity (IEIs) characterized by infection susceptibility, autoimmunity, inflammation, and lymphoproliferation. However, the core features of the gene-disease relationships underlying these conditions are often obscured by limitations in available published data. The Clinical Genome Resource (ClinGen) is an international collaborative effort that seeks to address this challenge for PIRDs and other monogenic diseases through a standardized framework for classifying the strength of gene-disease rela
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study applies the ClinGen gene-disease validity framework to systematically classify the strength of evidence linking genes to primary immune regulatory disorders (PIRDs), a growing subset of inborn errors of immunity. By standardizing how published data are evaluated, the work clarifies which gene-disease relationships are well-supported versus those limited by insufficient or conflicting evidence. The result is a curated landscape of genetic and phenotypic features that can guide clinical interpretation and future research in immune dysregulation.

papers.title: The CFDE Workbench: Integrating Metadata and Processed Data from Common Fund Programs.
papers.abstract: The NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) program was established to facilitate data accessibility and interoperability across multiple Common Fund (CF) programs, promote collaborations and accelerate discoveries by combining diverse data types from different CF programs. The CFDE Data Resource Center (DRC) was tasked with developing two web-based portals: an Information Portal to serve information about the CFDE, and a Data Portal to host harmonized metadata and processed data contributed by participating CF Data Coordination Centers (DCCs) and other sources. To achieve these goals, the CFDE
papers.summary: The CFDE Workbench is a web-based data portal that integrates harmonized metadata and processed data from multiple NIH Common Fund programs, enabling cross-program data discovery and interoperability. It provides a unified interface for researchers to access and combine diverse data types contributed by participating Data Coordination Centers.

papers.title: PDBe-KB Complexes: Enabling Functional Insight from Macromolecular Complexes in the PDB.
papers.abstract: PDBe-KB Complexes is a set of webpages that aggregate experimentally determined macromolecular assemblies into unique complex-level records within the Protein Data Bank in Europe Knowledge Base framework. Each unique complex identifier unifies equivalent biological assemblies from the PDB that represent the same macromolecular complex, consolidating information on component identity, stoichiometry, symmetry, ligands, and PISA-derived assembly properties within a consistent framework. Relationships between complexes are established by comparing their compositions, capturing both subcomplexes th
papers.summary: PDBe-KB Complexes is a new resource that aggregates experimentally determined macromolecular assemblies from the PDB into unique complex-level records, unifying equivalent biological assemblies and consolidating information on components, stoichiometry, symmetry, ligands, and assembly properties. It also captures relationships between complexes by comparing their compositions, including subcomplex relationships, enabling functional insight at the level of whole complexes rather than individual structures.

papers.title: HemOncAgent: an artificial intelligence system for retrieving structured and narrative oncology knowledge.
papers.abstract: Oncology knowledge spans structured and unstructured datasets of drugs, regimens, conditions, and identifiers, as well as clinician-authored narratives describing treatment sequencing across disease settings. Answering clinical questions may require accessing both databases and free-text narratives, but existing intelligent retrieval systems favor either relational facts or narrative context. We developed HemOncAgent, an artificial intelligence agent that selects among retrieval tools for the HemOnc knowledge ecosystem: HemOncKB, a curated knowledge graph for pharmacologic relationships, and H
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: HemOncAgent is an AI agent that answers oncology questions by dynamically choosing between a curated structured knowledge graph (HemOncKB) and free-text clinical narratives. This hybrid retrieval approach addresses the gap left by existing systems that handle either relational facts or narrative context, but not both. The system aims to support clinicians in navigating complex treatment sequencing and drug-regimen information.

papers.title: Utilization of advanced machine learning based on financial ontology induction for adaptive multilingual method in document recognition.
papers.abstract: A noise-robust framework is introduced for semi-supervised cross-lingual financial ontology induction, designed to address the challenges posed by noisy and partially labeled multilingual financial documents. The method employs a confidence-based filtering mechanism to eliminate low-quality cross-lingual text pairs, followed by multi-view distillation to harmonize linguistic and structural representations of financial entities. An uncertainty-aware contrastive learning objective further aligns entities across languages while reducing the influence of unreliable alignments. The resulting ontolo
papers.summary: The paper introduces a noise-robust machine learning framework for inducing financial ontologies across multiple languages from noisy, partially labeled documents. It uses confidence-based filtering, multi-view distillation, and uncertainty-aware contrastive learning to align financial entities across languages. The resulting ontology supports adaptive multilingual document recognition.

papers.title: Synergistic role of molecular imaging and genomics in thyroid cancer management: from diagnosis to personalized treatment.
papers.abstract: The management of thyroid cancer has advanced through the integration of molecular imaging, genomic profiling, and bioinformatics, supporting precision oncology across diverse subtypes. Although radioiodine imaging and therapy remain standard for differentiated thyroid cancers, efficacy can be limited in refractory cases due to heterogeneous iodine uptake. Advances including dosimetry-guided radioiodine therapy, hybrid imaging modalities (SPECT/CT, PET/CT, PET/MRI), and novel radiotracers (FDG, NaF) may improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic decision-making, particularly for aggressive tu
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining molecular imaging (such as PET/CT, SPECT/CT, and novel radiotracers) with genomic profiling and bioinformatics can improve the diagnosis and personalized treatment of thyroid cancer. It highlights that while radioiodine remains standard for differentiated thyroid cancers, integrating imaging and genomics may help overcome challenges like treatment resistance and heterogeneous iodine uptake in aggressive subtypes.

papers.title: Rabies Virus Glycoprotein G Variation Is Associated with Neurovirulence and Reduced Vamp2 Abundance in a Mouse Model of Direct CNS Infection.
papers.abstract: Rabies virus causes fatal neurological disease, but the mechanisms by which its glycoprotein G influences neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. In this study, we rescued two recombinant RABV LBNSE strains carrying G proteins from either the attenuated SAD-B19 strain or the virulent CVS11 strain, designated as rLBNSE-SfG and rLBNSE-CfG, respectively. Infection of primary mouse neurons and challenge experiments in mice showed that rLBNSE-CfG was associated with increased early neuronal infectivity and greater neurovirulence after intracerebral (i.c.) injection. Western blot analys
papers.summary: The study generated two recombinant rabies viruses differing only in their glycoprotein G (from attenuated SAD-B19 or virulent CVS11 strains) and compared their effects in mouse neurons and mice. The virulent G variant increased early neuronal infectivity and neurovirulence after direct CNS injection, and was linked to reduced abundance of the synaptic protein Vamp2. This suggests glycoprotein G variation contributes to rabies neurovirulence partly through disruption of synaptic vesicle machinery.

papers.title: Integrated Single Cell Analysis Reveals the Transcriptional Heterogeneity of Mouse Double Negative T Cells.
papers.abstract: Double negative T cells (DNT cells) are a rare T cell population involved in immune regulation, inflammation, autoimmunity, transplantation, and tumor immunity. However, their low abundance and dispersed distribution across tissues have limited a systematic understanding of their cellular organization and transcriptional diversity. To address this problem, we developed an integrative single cell framework to reconstruct the mouse DNT cell landscape across tissues using multiple public single cell RNA sequencing datasets. Using transcriptomic criteria, we identified and integrated 7984 mouse RN
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to reconstruct the transcriptional landscape of rare mouse double negative T (DNT) cells across tissues. The authors identify 7,984 DNT cells and characterize their transcriptional heterogeneity, providing a systematic resource for understanding this poorly studied immune population.

papers.title: MTB-KB: A Curated Knowledgebase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Related Studies.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), has regained its position as the world's leading killer among infectious diseases. Despite extensive research progress across epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, treatment regimens, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence factors, and immune mechanisms, MTB-related knowledge remains fragmented across thousands of publications, limiting its application in research and clinical practice. To address this gap, we present MTB-KB, a literature-curated knowledgebase that systematically integrates high-impact findings from eight major
papers.summary: MTB-KB is a manually curated knowledgebase that consolidates high-impact findings on Mycobacterium tuberculosis from thousands of publications, covering areas such as epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence, and immune mechanisms. It aims to overcome the fragmentation of TB-related knowledge and make it more accessible for both research and clinical applications.

papers.title: DHX15 as a novel immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer: An integrated bioinformatics analysis with in vitro functional validation.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a disease that occurs relatively frequently, and its prognosis and treatment outcomes are not optimal at present. Identifying novel BC biomarkers and therapeutic targets is key. DEAH-box helicase 15 (DHX15) is an RNA helicase that exhibits enhanced activity and is closely associated with tumorigenic potential. Alternative splicing is widely dysregulated in BC. However, the biological function of DHX15 in BC, in addition to its underlying molecular mechanisms, remain unclear. DHX15, a key RNA helicase involved in splicing regulation, was therefore selected to explore wheth
papers.summary: This study identifies DHX15, an RNA helicase involved in splicing regulation, as a potential immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer. Using integrated bioinformatics analysis combined with in vitro functional validation, the authors show that DHX15 expression is associated with tumorigenic potential and clinical outcomes. The work suggests DHX15 may serve as a novel therapeutic target, though validation remains preliminary.

papers.title: Methods for determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions to facilitate antimicrobial stewardship: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Effective antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) requires accurate information on the reason for prescribing antimicrobials. To design targeted interventions aimed at improving guideline adherence, accurate information on the indication for each prescription is necessary. This scoping review maps the existing methods used for systematically determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions.
papers.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
papers.summary: This scoping review maps existing methods for systematically determining the indication behind antibiotic prescriptions, a prerequisite for effective antimicrobial stewardship programs. It catalogs approaches used to capture prescribing rationale, aiming to inform targeted interventions that improve guideline adherence. The review highlights the current landscape and gaps in indication-tracking methodology.

papers.title: Re-emerging Marburg virus disease in Africa: spillover ecology, geographic expansion, and surveillance vulnerabilities.
papers.abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is re-emerging across Africa as a high-consequence zoonosis shaped by expanding ecological suitability, repeated spillover, and uneven surveillance capacity. This review synthesizes current evidence on the ecological, epidemiological, and operational determinants of contemporary Marburg virus (MARV) emergence. We conceptualize MVD as an ecological-emergence system produced by interactions among reservoir-host biology, environmental change, human exposure, health-system readiness, and mobility, rather than as a series of isolated outbreaks. Recent detections in multi
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the re-emergence of Marburg virus disease across Africa, framing outbreaks as an ecological-emergence system driven by reservoir-host biology, environmental change, human exposure, health-system readiness, and mobility rather than isolated events. It highlights expanding ecological suitability, repeated spillovers, and uneven surveillance capacity as key determinants of contemporary emergence.

papers.title: Beyond the autonomous individual: hydrosocial relations and the constitution of the relational hydrosocial self in an Andean conflict.
papers.abstract: This article addresses a specific under-theorized problem in social theory: how subjectivity is constituted through relations in which ecological and nonhuman entities are not contextual but constitutive. Against dominant models that define the self as autonomous, bounded, and human-centered, it argues that subject formation can emerge through hydrosocial relations linking humans, water systems, territory, and nonhuman entities. Drawing on qualitative fieldwork in the Razuhuillca micro-watershed in the Peruvian Andes, the study combines in-depth interviews, walking ethnography, field observati
papers.summary: This qualitative sociological study examines how human subjectivity is shaped through relationships with water systems, territory, and nonhuman entities in the Razuhuillca micro-watershed of the Peruvian Andes. Using interviews, walking ethnography, and field observation, it argues against autonomous, human-centered models of the self, proposing instead a 'relational hydrosocial self' constituted through ecological relations. The work is a theoretical and ethnographic contribution to social theory rather than a data-driven or computational study.

papers.title: ApoA2 isoforms as blood-based biomarkers reflecting pancreatic exocrine dysfunction for risk stratification and perioperative management of pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: Apolipoprotein A2 isoforms (apoA2‑i) are clinically validated blood‑based biomarkers for the auxiliary diagnosis of pancreatic cancer. Emerging evidence also suggests that apoA2‑i may contribute to the detection of early‑stage pancreatic cancer, particularly in cohorts where CA19‑9 shows limited sensitivity, although these applications remain investigational and require prospective validation. Beyond diagnostic applications, apoA2‑i reflect pancreatic exocrine physiology, linking biomarker biology with perioperative outcomes such as postoperative pancreatic fistula and steatotic liver disease.
papers.summary: This review discusses apolipoprotein A2 isoforms (apoA2-i) as blood-based biomarkers for pancreatic cancer, highlighting their potential to detect early-stage disease where CA19-9 sensitivity is limited. It also proposes that apoA2-i reflect pancreatic exocrine function, making them useful for predicting perioperative complications like postoperative pancreatic fistula and steatotic liver disease.

papers.title: Grand challenge in microbiome data science: recovering the microbiome as a system.
papers.summary: This perspective piece frames the recovery of the microbiome as an integrated system—rather than a collection of taxa—as a grand challenge for microbiome data science. It argues that current analytical approaches often reduce complex community data to descriptive taxonomic profiles, and calls for new computational frameworks that capture ecological interactions, dynamics, and functional interdependence. The paper outlines conceptual and methodological directions needed to move the field toward systems-level understanding.
